name: Pre-Deployment Testing
summary: Government institutes and independent evaluators test each frontier model before its release, with enough time and access.
description: Outside testers find risks that the lab did not look for, and governments learn about capabilities before the public gets them. Testing after release cannot stop a dangerous release.

criteria.label: Government Access
criteria.description: A government AI institute (such as US CAISI or UK AISI) tests the model before release.

criteria.label: Third-Party Access
criteria.description: Independent evaluators test the model before release.

criteria.label: Every Frontier Model
criteria.description: Each new frontier model gets this testing, not only selected models.

criteria.label: Adequate Time
criteria.description: Testers get a stated time before release (weeks, not days) and access to versions with fewer safeguards.

criteria.label: Results Published
criteria.description: The findings, or a summary of them, are published with what the testers could not test.

orgs.summary: OpenAI gives US CAISI and outside testers its models before release under agreements; testing time is not fixed, and some tests last days.

events.title: Joins White House pledge on external red-teaming
events.summary: Agrees to internal and external red-teaming, with independent domain experts, for all major public releases of new frontier models, and to publish reports with adversarial testing results.

quote.text: Companies commit to advancing this area of research, and to developing a multi-faceted, specialized, and detailed red-teaming regime, including drawing on independent domain experts, for all major public releases of new models within scope.
